results.name: https-www-acma-gov-au-broadcasting-licence-areas
results.notes:
The _Broadcasting Services Act 1992_ mandates that Commercial and Community broadcasting services are licensed to serve specific geographic areas. 
These geographic areas are referred to as **Licence Areas**, and are determined by the Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) in Licence Area Plans (LAPs). 
The ACMA defines Licence Areas in terms of areas defined by the
[Australian Bureau of Statistics](http://www.abs.gov.au/) (ABS) for the
purposes of the Australian Census. The smallest area unit currently defined
by the ABS is the Collection District (CD).

This dataset comprises the collection of current broadcast Licence Areas, and
is made available in five forms:

  * the list of Australian Bureau of Statistics CD numbers making up the Licence Area definition, distributed in a comma separated value (CSV) format text file;
  * a translation of the ABS CD numbers into the names of the Local Government Areas (LGAs) and Statistical Division (SDs) within the area boundary, known as the Licence Area Description, rendered as an HTML page;
  * a geographic map displaying the Licence Area, distributed as a Portable Document Format (PDF) file;
  * a spatial dataset for use in GIS software, distributed as a ZIP archive containing ESRI Shapefile Format data files; and
  * a Google Earth Placemark (.KMZ) file viewable in the Google Earth application and other software that can display Placemark data.

results.name: water-licence-information
results.notes:
Water Licence Information is a spatial index of points representing the location of the offtake points for water allocations granted under the Water Management Act 1999.
Attributes for the Water Licence Information layer include the Water Licence Number, the name of the water Licence Holder, and a unique Allocation ID. 
The Period Amount for the allocation represents the volume of water  in Megalitres that may be taken between the Allocation Start Date and the Allocation End Date and the purpose for which the water may be used. 
The Surety Level represents the access priority of the allocation with Surety level 1 having the highest priority and Surety level 8 the lowest. Allocation Status is recorded along with the Name of the Water Resource from which the allocation may be taken. 
The Offtake ID is the identifier for the offtake where the allocation is taken and these have Offtake Easting and an Offtake Northing which use GDA 94. 
The records also note whether or not there is a Financial interest recorded against the water allocation

Location of all current Exploration Licences/Permits issued under the Petroleum Act, 2000, Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1982, or Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1967 for the regulated resource or commodity of petroleum. results.notes:
## **Abstract** 

This dataset and its metadata statement were supplied to the Bioregional Assessment Programme by a third party and are presented here as originally supplied. 

Location of all current Exploration Licence/Permit Applications issued under the Petroleum Act, 2000, Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1982, or Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1967 for the regulated resource or commodity of petroleum. Exploration Licences/Permits provide exclusive tenure rights to explore for the regulated resource or commodity of petroleum for a minimum of 5 or 6 years. Comment is sought on applications for Exploration Licences/Permits from numerous sources before granting. Exploration programs are subject to strict environmental and heritage conditions. Exploitation of identified resources must be made under separate petroleum production leases.

## **Purpose** 

The dataset was developed to record information necessary for the administration of the Petroleum Act, 2000, Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1982, and Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act, 1967.



Use: Used to supply government, industry and the general public with an up-to-date status and extent of petroleum exploration activities throughout the state.

## **Dataset History** 

Source Data History: Exploration Licence/Permit Application boundaries were sourced from the official Petroleum Register licence/permit application documents. Licence/permit application boundaries are legally defined to follow lines of latitude and longitude, based on potentially several geodetic datums.



Processing Steps: Coordinates entered by keyboard from licence/permit application documents. Non GDA94 coordinates transformed into GDA94. Linework cleaned to remove duplicate arcs. Data adjusted for accurate state border and coastline. Where appropriate cadastral parcels removed from licence/permit application polygons. Associated attribute data also captured from licence/permit application documents.

## **Dataset Citation** 

SA Department of Primary Industries and Resources (2013) SA Petroleum Exploration Licence/Permit Applications. Bioregional Assessment Source Dataset. Viewed 12 December 2018, http://data.bioregionalassessments.gov.au/dataset/d5667303-96c8-473f-af05-d3f53ac7753c.

## **Abstract** 

The dataset was derived by the Bioregional Assessment Programme from tabulated surface water data provided by the NSW Office of Water. The source datasets are identified in the Lineage field in this metadata statement. The processes undertaken to produce this derived dataset are described in the History field in this metadata statement.



It provides the geographical location of surface water licences within the Namoi subregion of the Northern Inland Catchments Bioregion. It is in a shapefile format and includes description on the purpose, volume and water source of each licence.

## **Purpose** 

To estimate locations and, purpose, water source and volumes associated with surface water licences.

## **Dataset History** 

The dataset was created by using tabulated coordinates of the surface water licence which were further displayed in Arc Map. The bioregion boundaries shapefile was used to intersect the licences locations which were thereafter exported into a shapefile.

This dataset contains Queensland's limousine and taxi service licence values, including licence type, transfer values and locations. 

The information published in this register includes transfer prices of taxi service licences and limousine licences. In December 2024 a complete review was undertaken to remove duplicate entries and anomalies to ensure data integrity and accuracy. Please disregard all previous versions.

The values may not always reflect ‘arms length’ transactions. For example, some transfers may be the result of a sale of partnership or organisational name change. In instances where a licence is transferred as a result of a business name change or a deceased estate, the licence value reflected in the register may be zero. In the case of taxi service licences, where the value of a licence transfer appears lower than average for that period, it may be the case that there were special conditions (for example – an owner/driver condition) imposed upon the licence at that time. 

The Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) plays no part in commercial transactions between private parties and does not determine the market value of any taxi service licence or limousine licence. 

The information published in this register is public information. Further enquiries about the information must be directed to The Department of Transport and Main Roads Right to Information Unit. results.notes:
## **Abstract** 

The dataset was derived by the Bioregional Assessment Programme. This dataset was derived from multiple datasets. You can find a link to the parent datasets in the Lineage Field in this metadata statement. The History Field in this metadata statement describes how this dataset was derived.



Preliminary analysis showed there were no bores from the QLD licence entitlement data extracted for Economic Assets in the top part of the CLM PAE (QLD section of the PAE). Discussions were held with Queensland Department of Resources and Mines validated that there were bores in this area that did not require a licence.

An investigation of the National Groundwater Information System (NGIS) showed that there were indeed approximately 2,400 bores identified as "functioning".

This dataset represents a selection of functioning QLD Bores from NGIS (GUID:e157b1cd-3cb7-4cf9-a13c-a6bed576b8c7) clipped by the CLM PAE and assumed to be unlicenced in QLD. Inclusion of Bores in the CLM PAE that were without licences but were "functioning" bores.

## **Purpose** 

Please note there is NO known "purpose" information for these bores and in the abscence of this information they have been classfied "Basic Water Right" in the sub group "Groundwater management zone or area (surface area)". There is also NO known volume of entitlment or take associated with these bores, though there are several methodologies of how this could be allocated.

## **Dataset History** 

Dataset was created within ESRI ArcMap 10.1 by selecting all bores from QLD that were functioning from the Bureau of Meteorology National Groundwater Iinformation System database.

("NGIS_Bore_StateTerritory" = 4-QLD AND "NGIS_Bore_Status" = 'FUN')



These bores were then clipped using the CLM PAE  and a field was added to the dataset "ASSET_CLASS" and populated with "Basic Water Rights".  An extra field was added SubGoup and populated with "Groundwater management zone or area (surface area)".
